# shaderange

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

The shaderange package helps beauty product strategy managers decide where their next foundation launch could make the biggest difference. It compares the deep, medium and light shades a brand offers at Sephora and Ulta with the whole market, showing where the brand’s range is thinner than its competitors’ and where the market as a whole is thin. For each gap, it points to the competitor products that currently lead, giving a benchmark to catch up to or a chance to stand out.

The package contains:

- `foundation_shades`: 6,774 foundation shades from 107 brands, collected
  from the Sephora and Ulta websites in early 2021
- `shade_supply()`: summarises shade supply by lightness band
- `brand_gaps()`: compares a brand's shade mix with the market
- `run_app()`: launches an interactive Shiny app for exploring brand gaps

Documentation website: <https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-miriam0085/>

## Installation

Install the package from GitHub with:

``` r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-miriam0085")
```

## Launch the app

``` r
library(shaderange)
run_app()
```

Choose your brand and retailer in the sidebar. The app shows where your
brand's shade mix is thinner than the market and which competitor products
lead those bands.

## Example

Compare a brand's shade mix with the market:

```{r example}
library(shaderange)
brand_gaps(foundation_shades, brand = "L'Oréal")
```

A negative `gap` marks a band where the brand offers proportionally fewer
shades than the market.

## Data

The shade data come from The Pudding's article
[The Naked Truth](https://pudding.cool/2021/03/foundation-names/) (2021),
released under the MIT licence and accessed via
[TidyTuesday](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2021/2021-03-30).
The script data-raw/foundation_shades.R downloads the raw data from TidyTuesday, removes duplicate shades and saves the cleaned result as foundation_shades.
